title: Spatial Cross-Validation & Geographic Leakage
interviewAnswer: Random splits can overestimate geospatial model performance because nearby samples are correlated; spatial blocking or leave-region-out validation better measures transfer to new areas.
why: Spatial data can make test examples near-duplicates of training examples.
intuition: If deployment is a new city, validation should mimic a new city—not random points from the same streets.
deepDive: Block scale should reflect autocorrelation range and deployment scope; performance can be reported by region and distance from training support.
commonMistakes: Using blocks too small to break dependence.
production: Design validation around geographic deployment and monitor regional performance.
workedExample: Hold out whole farms/regions for crop prediction instead of random pixels from each farm.

visual.title: Spatial validation holds out coherent regions
visual.caption: Conceptually, geographic blocks separate train and test instead of randomly mixing neighbors.
